# `silk/http_target`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Profiles: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`.

HTTP request-target forms, authority validation, URI conversion, and Host selection.

## When to use

Use [`RequestTarget.parse`](#declaration-73696c6b2f687474705f7461726765743a3a526571756573745461726765742e7061727365) for received or already serialized targets and [`RequestTarget.fromUri`](#declaration-73696c6b2f687474705f7461726765743a3a526571756573745461726765742e66726f6d557269)
for outgoing origin- or absolute-form bytes. Use [`validateRequestHost`](#declaration-73696c6b2f687474705f7461726765743a3a76616c696461746552657175657374486f7374) before server routing.

## Details

Parsing preserves accepted spelling and percent escapes. URI conversion deliberately omits a
fragment, while raw target parsing rejects one. No operation resolves DNS or connects.

Import as `RequestTarget` with `import silk.http_target { RequestTarget }`.
